title: BBQ Meatball Skewers
shortDescription: Glazed beef meatballs on skewers with quick slaw for ten
subtitle: Glazed beef meatballs on skewers with quick slaw for ten
description: Seasoned beef meatballs are baked, glazed with sticky BBQ sauce, and threaded onto skewers with pickled onions and cherry tomatoes. A quick vinegar slaw on the side keeps the bite balanced.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for BBQ Meatball Skewers in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Mix and roll meatballs
steps.instruction: Combine beef, breadcrumbs, eggs, garlic powder, onion powder, and salt until just mixed. Roll into 40 equal meatballs about 1.5 inches across for two per skewer. Plan about 15 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Bake the meatballs
steps.instruction: Arrange on a wire rack over a sheet pan. Bake at 425°F for 18–20 minutes until browned and internal temp reaches 160°F in the center. Target oven/smoker temperature: 425°F. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Glaze and finish
steps.instruction: Brush generously with BBQ sauce and bake 5 more minutes at 425°F until glaze sets sticky. Internal temp should still read at least 160°F after glazing. Target oven/smoker temperature: 425°F. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Quick slaw
steps.instruction: Toss cabbage with apple cider vinegar, a tablespoon of oil, salt, and pepper. Drain excess liquid so slaw stays crisp on the platter. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Skewer and serve
steps.instruction: Thread two meatballs, a tomato, and pickled onion on each skewer. Arrange on a platter with slaw cups for grabbing between plays. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Wet hands when rolling meatballs—they stick less and stay round.
Reduce BBQ sauce by half before glazing if store sauce is thin and runs off.
Swap beef for half turkey if you want lighter skewers without changing the format.
tonightSpread: BBQ meatball skewers with slaw cups and extra glaze for dunking.
Cornbread muffins for crews who want something sweet alongside smoky meatballs.
leftovers: Slide meatballs off skewers into sub rolls with extra slaw.
Chop into a rice bowl with the slaw and hot sauce.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Skewers turn meatballs into portable game food without buns getting soggy. They reheat in minutes and look intentional on a platter—not like leftover spaghetti night.
mealPrepNotes: Roll meatballs uniform so they bake evenly. Soak wooden skewers 30 minutes if grilling for presentation. Glaze can be reduced ahead for a thicker stick.
